comments.author: @gianlucazucca1322
comments.text: The framing "British, Swiss, Austrian and French climbers" doesn't hold up either way. If we're talking about the first ascents of the 4000ers during the Golden Age (1854-65), that's British climbers with Swiss, French and Italian guides (Carrel and Bich on the Matterhorn's Italian side, 17 July 1865), and Austrians don't belong on the list. If instead we want to include Austrians, we're talking about the 1920s-30s and the great north faces, and then Germans and Italians have to be named too: the Schmid brothers on the Matterhorn north face (1931), Comici and the Dimai brothers on the Cima Grande north face (1933), Cassin and his partners on the Badile (1937) and the Walker Spur (1938), and the mixed German-Austrian team on the Eiger (1938).
